content: Lobelia, also referred to as Indian Tobacco, Asthma Weed, Pukeweed, or Vomitwort, belongs to the plant family Campanulaceae and includes over 400 species. Some of these species, such as Lobelia cardinalis (commonly known as Cardinal Flower or Indian Pink), Lobelia siphilitica (Blue Lobelia), Lobelia fulgens, and Lobelia erinus, are cultivated for ornamental purposes in gardens. Additionally, hybrids of these species are also grown. Certain botanists classify the genus Lobelia and its related plants under a separate family, Lobeliaceae, although the Angiosperm Phylogeny Group has not definitively resolved this classification, listing the genus under both families. Lobelia erinus, an annual plant native to South Africa, is frequently used in decorative settings such as window boxes and hanging baskets. Numerous varieties of this species have been developed, showcasing a wide range of colors. Lobelia is considered a foundational genus from which many other lobelioid genera have evolved. However, it is highly paraphyletic, meaning it does not form a cohesive evolutionary group, and thus is not considered a well-defined genus. For instance, Hawaiian species of Lobelia are part of a broader group that includes other genera with significantly different appearances (referred to as Hawaiian lobelioids). Despite this, the group is not sufficiently understood to warrant a reclassification. Lobelia species serve as food sources for the larvae of certain Lepidoptera species, such as the Setaceous Hebrew Character moth. The genus is named after Matthias de Lobel, a Belgian botanist who lived from 1538 to 1616. In the Victorian language of flowers, Lobelia symbolizes malevolence and ill will. Medicinal Use Historically, Native Americans utilized Lobelia to address respiratory and muscular disorders and as a purgative. In modern times, Lobelia is employed in the treatment of asthma and food poisoning and is often included in smoking cessation programs. It acts as a physical relaxant and can function as a nerve depressant, alleviating tension and panic. The species most commonly used in contemporary herbal medicine is Lobelia inflata (Indian Tobacco). In North America, Lobelia is recognized for its medicinal properties, which include being an emetic (inducing vomiting), stimulant, antispasmodic, expectorant, diaphoretic (promoting sweating), relaxant, nauseant, sedative, diuretic, and nervine (calming the nerves). However, due to its similarity to nicotine, the internal use of Lobelia can pose risks, particularly to vulnerable populations such as children, pregnant women, and individuals with cardiac conditions. Overuse of Lobelia can result in nausea and vomiting. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy and should ideally be administered under the guidance of a qualified practitioner. Two species, Lobelia siphilitica and Lobelia cardinalis, were historically believed to be cures for syphilis. In the early 1800s, herbalist Samuel Thompson popularized the medicinal use of Lobelia in the United States, along with other plants like goldenseal. One species, Lobelia chinensis (known as 半边莲 or bàn biān lián in Chinese), is considered one of the 50 fundamental herbs in traditional Chinese medicine. Selected Species The genus Lobelia includes numerous species, such as: Lobelia aberdarica Lobelia anatina (Southwestern Blue Lobelia) Lobelia appendiculata Lobelia inflata (Indian Tobacco) Lobelia erinus (Edging Lobelia, Annual Lobelia, Trailing Lobelia) Lobelia siphilitica (Blue Lobelia) Lobelia cardinalis (Cardinal Flower) Lobelia chinensis (used in traditional Chinese medicine) Lobelia dortmanna Lobelia tupa Lobelia nicotianifolia Lobelia purpurascens (Purple Lobelia) This list represents only a selection of the many species within the genus.
